sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
We have already implemented a tool-calling loop using pure Python. Now we can understand what an agent framework abstracts.

LangChain provides a higher-level agent runtime through `create_agent`, with tools and configurable middleware. citeturn228516view0

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments. We have already implemented a tool-calling loop using pure Python.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

sections.title: 11.1 Installation
sections.body:
```bash
pip install -U langchain langchain-openai
```

For production deployments, pin tested dependency versions rather than installing unbounded upgrades.

sections.title: 11.2 Basic LangChain agent
11.3 Pure Python vs LangChain vs LangGraph
sections.body:
| Capability | Pure Python | LangChain | LangGraph |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Direct execution control | High | Abstracted | High |
| Tool-calling abstraction | Implement yourself | Built in | Configurable |
| Custom control flow | Implement yourself | Middleware and composition | Explicit graph |
| Persistent checkpoints | Implement yourself | Configurable | Core capability |
| Human approval workflows | Implement yourself | Middleware | Interrupts |
| Learning difficulty | Basic initially | Moderate | Higher |
| Suitable use case | Small specialized runtime | Standard tool-calling agents | Complex stateful orchestration |

Frameworks do not automatically make an application production-ready. They provide abstractions that still need security controls, testing, resource limits and deployment engineering.

steps.label: Orchestrator
steps.narration: A coordinator decomposes work and assigns ownership to specialists.

steps.label: Delegate
steps.narration: Tasks are handed off with clear inputs, outputs, and termination conditions.

steps.label: Specialists
steps.narration: Specialist agents execute narrow skills and return structured results.

steps.label: Merge
steps.narration: Results are reconciled; conflicts and duplicates are resolved before final output.

steps.label: Terminate
steps.narration: The workflow must always end — via success, safe failure, timeout, or human decision.
